questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: I wanted to ameliorate my linguistic competences

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The distance to my home country, the culture and the language

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I can only recommend going on an exchange to Humboldt University in Berlin. It was an amazing experience on all levels.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, I got all the information I needed per mail.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The international team at my host university were very helpful with all the administrative steps when arriving in the country and registering at the university.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was very lucky to know a place I could rent, but in general it's pretty complicated to find housing in Berlin. I would recommend not being picky about the distance to the center of the city and to consider private dorms even though they are quite expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You will still make friends through your classes and language courses!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I don't have a say about this, as I was very lucky.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was an introductory zoom meeting explaining everything. However, it was a bit confusing and took some time to get the student card which you needed to use public transportation.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: At some point, you receive a letter with a pin code. When you have received this letter, you have to book a meeting at the international office, where they deliver you your student card, and then you have to activate it with the pin code.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The international office answers all of your questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I asked for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient, and make sure you get through all the necessary steps.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a wide range of classes in several languages (German, English, French, Chinese and so on), and they were very interesting.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses from the 1st, 3rd and 7th year, and I found the level appropriate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. The style of teaching in Berlin is very old school with a teacher making a lecture and the students listening and taking notes. There was very little group work or group presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
-Staatsrecht mit Bezügen zum Völker- und Europarecht
-Europäische Wirtschaftsrecht
-Internetrecht
-Méthodologie juridique francaise
-Droits fondamentaux et leur protection juridictionelle en droit francais
-Model European Union Conference

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would strongly recommend the English classes, as they are very easy to follow, as well as the German Völkerrecht-classes, as I've heard they're really good! The Europäische Wirtschaftsrecht was also super interesting.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Tips when going out in cafés, bars, restaurants, even clubs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
It wasn't as cheap as expected to go groceries shopping, but going out in restaurants and bars was extremely cheap.
Clubs can both be super cheap and pretty expensive.
There is a lot of cultural offers for students making museums, theaters and operas very affordable.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was a lot of different sports, you could go to - something for everyone!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There was a lot of different sports, you could go to - something for everyone!
The international office also organized some meet-ups and creative/cultural events.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend going to museums, theaters, bars and in general just to explore the culture of the city.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It's easy to go to short trips to cities like Potsdam, Hamburg or even Prague and Breslau.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Take classes in German and talk to the Germans! They are very nice and friendly

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You have to be very polite when adressing teachers in e-mails.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The diversity and openmindedness.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Take the classes you are the most interested in
2. Make sure to respect the deadlines
3. Use the Mensa (school canteen!). Very cheap and great opportunity to meet people.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try as many classes as you can in the first two weeks. And try to be punctual.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting all the people I've met, exploring Berlin, learning German and studying at Humboldt.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To sleep enough.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
